name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q01 - Animal husbandry dairying apiculture and fisheries

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding animal husbandry practices:

Statement I: Fisheries include rearing, catching, and selling of fish, molluscs (shell-fish), and crustaceans (prawns, crabs, etc.).

Statement II: In dairy farm management, regular inspections with proper record keeping and mandatory regular visits by a veterinary doctor help identify and rectify problems early.

Statement III: Apis indica is the most common species of honeybee reared in India, and bee-keeping is not labour-intensive.

Statement IV: Aquaculture and pisciculture have been employed to increase the production of both freshwater and marine aquatic plants and animals, contributing to the Blue Revolution.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal husbandry encompasses livestock care, dairy management, apiculture, and fisheries, applying scientific management to boost food production.

Step 2: Evaluation of Fisheries and Dairy Management
Fisheries cover the rearing, catching, processing, and selling of fish, molluscs (shell-fish), and crustaceans (prawns, crabs). In dairy farm management, stringent hygiene, regular inspections with proper record keeping, and mandatory periodic visits by a veterinary doctor ensure early detection and rectification of health or production issues. Thus, both claims are true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Apiculture and the Blue Revolution
Apis indica is the most commonly reared honeybee species, and bee-keeping is not labour-intensive and can be practised in courtyards, verandahs, or roofs. Similarly, aquaculture and pisciculture have expanded the production of freshwater and marine aquatic organisms, driving the Blue Revolution alongside the Green Revolution. Thus, both of these claims are also true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four claims accurately describe the scope of fisheries, dairy farm management, apiculture, and the Blue Revolution.

answer.text: All four statements are correct.
Only Statements I, II, and III are correct.
Only Statements II, III, and IV are correct.
Only Statements I and IV are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q02 - Inbreeding out-crossing artificial insemination and MOET

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding animal breeding and controlled breeding technologies:

Statement I: Inbreeding exposes harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection and helps in the accumulation of superior genes.

Statement II: Out-crossing is the best breeding method for animals that are below average in productivity in milk production or growth rate in beef cattle.

Statement III: In artificial insemination, collected semen must always be used immediately and cannot be frozen or transported to distant farms.

Statement IV: Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET) has been demonstrated for cattle, sheep, rabbits, buffaloes, and mares to increase herd size in a short time.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal breeding uses controlled mating strategies—inbreeding, out-crossing, artificial insemination, and MOET—to improve genetic merit and reproductive efficiency.

Step 2: Evaluation of Inbreeding and Out-crossing
Inbreeding increases homozygosity, exposing harmful recessive alleles for elimination by selection while accumulating superior genes. Out-crossing (mating unrelated animals of the same breed with no common ancestors for 4–6 generations) is the best method for animals below average in milk productivity or beef cattle growth rate. Thus, both of these claims are true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Artificial Insemination and MOET
In artificial insemination, semen collected from a chosen male may be used immediately or frozen for later use and transported in frozen form to where the female is housed; claiming it cannot be frozen or transported is false. Meanwhile, MOET has indeed been demonstrated in cattle, sheep, rabbits, buffaloes, and mares to rapidly increase herd size, making that claim true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding inbreeding, out-crossing, and MOET applications are correct, whereas the restriction claimed for artificial insemination semen storage and transport is incorrect.

answer.text: All four statements are correct.
Only Statements I, II, and IV are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.
Only Statements II, III, and IV are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q03 - Plant breeding steps sugarcane and millet hybrids

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements about plant breeding and Indian hybrid crops:

Statement I: Classical plant breeding involves crossing pure lines followed solely by natural selection without human intervention.

Statement II: During selection and testing of superior recombinants, selected plants are self-pollinated for several generations until they reach homozygosity so that characters do not segregate in the progeny.

Statement III: Crossing north Indian Saccharum barberi with south Indian Saccharum officinarum produced sugarcane varieties combining high yield, thick stems, high sugar, and adaptability to north India.

Statement IV: Hybrid breeding in millets such as maize, jowar, and bajra has failed to produce high-yielding varieties resistant to water stress.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant breeding is the purposeful manipulation of plant species through hybridisation, artificial selection, and progeny selfing to stabilise desirable traits.

Step 2: Evaluation of Classical Plant Breeding and Recombinant Selfing
Classical plant breeding involves crossing or hybridisation of pure lines followed by artificial selection (not natural selection) to obtain desirable traits, making the first claim false. After selecting superior recombinants, plants are self-pollinated for several generations until they attain uniformity (homozygosity) so traits do not segregate in progeny, making the second claim true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Sugarcane and Millet Hybrids
Saccharum barberi (north India, poor sugar and yield) was crossed with Saccharum officinarum (south India, thick stems and high sugar) to combine high yield, thick stems, high sugar, and north Indian adaptability, making the third claim true. In contrast, hybrid breeding in maize, jowar, and bajra has successfully developed high-yielding varieties resistant to water stress, making the fourth claim false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Only the claims describing self-pollination to achieve homozygosity in superior recombinants and the interspecific sugarcane hybridisation are correct.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements I, III, and IV are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
Only Statements II, III, and IV are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q04 - Disease and insect pest resistance in crops

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding breeding for disease and insect pest resistance:

Statement I: Brown rust of wheat, red rot of sugarcane, and late blight of potato are caused by fungi, whereas black rot of crucifers is caused by bacteria.

Statement II: In mung bean, resistance to bacterial blight and white rust was induced through mutation breeding.

Statement III: Hairy leaves in cotton provide resistance to bollworms, while solid stems in wheat lead to non-preference by jassids.

Statement IV: Pusa Shubhra and Pusa Snowball K-1 are cauliflower varieties resistant to black rot and curl blight black rot, whereas Pusa Sem 2 and Pusa Sem 3 are flat bean varieties resistant to jassids, aphids, and fruit borer.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Breeding for biotic stress resistance targets specific fungal, bacterial, and viral pathogens as well as morphological or biochemical deterrents against insect pests.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pathogens and Mutation Breeding
Rusts (such as brown rust of wheat), red rot of sugarcane, and late blight of potato are fungal diseases, while black rot of crucifers is bacterial; thus, the first claim is true. In mung bean, artificial mutation breeding induced resistance to yellow mosaic virus and powdery mildew—not bacterial blight and white rust—making the second claim false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Insect Resistance Traits and Released Varieties
Hairy leaves in cotton confer resistance to jassids (while smooth-leaved, nectar-less cotton deters bollworms), and solid stems in wheat confer non-preference by the stem sawfly (not jassids); thus, the third claim is false. On the other hand, Pusa Shubhra and Pusa Snowball K-1 are cauliflower varieties resistant to black rot and curl blight black rot, and Pusa Sem 2 and Pusa Sem 3 are flat bean varieties resistant to jassids, aphids, and fruit borer, making the fourth claim true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Only the claims identifying fungal/bacterial crop diseases and the released cauliflower and flat bean resistant varieties are correct.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and III are correct.
Only Statements I, III, and IV are correct.
Only Statements I and IV are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q05 - Biofortification hidden hunger and single cell protein

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding biofortification and Single Cell Protein (SCP):

Statement I: About 840 million people in the world suffer from micronutrient, protein, and vitamin deficiencies, a condition referred to as hidden hunger.

Statement II: An iron-fortified rice variety has been developed containing over five times as much iron as in commonly consumed varieties.

Statement III: Spirulina is a microscopic fungus that requires pure glucose medium and cannot grow on waste water or sewage.

Statement IV: The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi has released iron and calcium enriched spinach and bathua, as well as protein enriched broad, lablab, French, and garden peas.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biofortification enhances the nutritional density of staple crops and vegetables, while Single Cell Protein (SCP) utilises fast-growing microbes on low-cost substrates to supply protein.

Step 2: Evaluation of Hidden Hunger and Iron-Fortified Rice
More than 840 million people lack adequate daily food, whereas a far greater number—three billion people—suffer from micronutrient, protein, and vitamin deficiencies known as hidden hunger; thus, equating hidden hunger with 840 million people is false. Conversely, an iron-fortified rice variety containing over five times as much iron as commonly consumed varieties has been developed, making that claim true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Spirulina and IARI Biofortified Vegetables
Spirulina is a blue-green alga (not a microscopic fungus) that grows easily on potato processing waste water, straw, molasses, animal manure, and sewage, reducing environmental pollution; hence, the claim about Spirulina is false. Finally, IARI, New Delhi has released iron and calcium enriched spinach and bathua, along with protein enriched beans (broad, lablab, French, and garden peas), making that claim true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Only the claims describing the iron-fortified rice variety and the IARI-released mineral- and protein-enriched vegetables are correct.

answer.text: Only Statements I and II are correct.
Only Statements II and IV are correct.
Only Statements I, II, and IV are correct.
Only Statements II, III, and IV are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q06 - Explants nutrient media meristem culture and somatic hybrids

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding plant tissue culture and its applications:

Statement I: Any part of a plant taken out and grown in a test tube under sterile conditions in special nutrient media to regenerate a whole plant is called an explant.

Statement II: For successful in vitro propagation of an explant, the nutrient medium requires only inorganic salts and water, without any carbon source or growth regulators.

Statement III: Scientists have succeeded in culturing apical and axillary meristems of banana, sugarcane, and potato to obtain virus-free plants from virus-infected plants.

Statement IV: Somatic hybridisation involves digesting plant cell walls to isolate naked protoplasts surrounded by plasma membranes and fusing protoplasts from two different varieties, as demonstrated in pomato.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant tissue culture relies on totipotency under aseptic conditions with defined media, enabling micro-propagation, meristem culture for virus elimination, and protoplast fusion for somatic hybridisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Explants and Nutrient Medium Requirements
An explant is any part of a plant excised and grown in a sterile test tube on special nutrient media to regenerate a whole plant, making the first claim true. However, the nutrient medium must supply a carbon source such as sucrose, inorganic salts, vitamins, amino acids, and growth regulators like auxins and cytokinins; claiming only inorganic salts and water are needed is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Meristem Culture and Somatic Hybridisation
Even in virus-infected plants, apical and axillary meristems remain virus-free, and culturing them in vitro has yielded virus-free banana, sugarcane, and potato plants, making the third claim true. Additionally, isolating naked protoplasts (bounded by plasma membranes) by cell-wall digestion and fusing protoplasts from two varieties produces somatic hybrids—such as pomato from tomato and potato—making the fourth claim true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims defining explants, meristem culture in banana/sugarcane/potato, and somatic hybridisation via protoplast fusion are correct, whereas omitting the carbon source and growth regulators from the nutrient medium is incorrect.

answer.text: All four statements are correct.
Only Statements I and III are correct.
Only Statements I, III, and IV are correct.
Only Statements II, III, and IV are correct.
